claims.text: Section 3(p) of the Indian Patents Act expressly excludes an invention that is traditional knowledge or an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known components from patentability.

This directly supports the claim that Section 3(p) excludes traditional knowledge from patentability, and consequently, traditional knowledge itself cannot be patented in India.

Benefits of the PCT
Using the PCT to seek patent protection for your invention internationally can be advantageous in many respects.
First, it is
more convenient
than filing separate national patent applications in multiple countries, as your single PCT application is recognized in all Contracting States as having the same effect as a national application.

more time
